title: Homeward
summary: A source-grounded hospital discharge assistant that coordinates patient tasks, caregiver follow-up, specialist routing, and human approval.
landingDeck: Homeward turns a discharge packet into an agent-supported recovery workflow with source retrieval, specialist routing, approval, and retry states.
landingHighlights: Turns a dense discharge packet into a patient-centered recovery view.
Routes source search and specialist tasks through explicit human review and escalation.
Shows source provenance, reviewer approval, activity history, and safe retry states on screen.
problem: Discharge plans arrive when patients and caregivers are tired, anxious, and responsible for coordinating medications, appointments, warning signs, and follow-up care.
approach: Homeward combines document-grounded retrieval, task routing, specialist workflows, source provenance, and explicit human review around one fictional patient journey.
output: A team-built prototype with source search, four bounded specialist roles, approval and recovery states, 59 Node tests, four DOM journeys, and 32 deterministic evaluation cases at the assessed commit.

methodology.evaluation: At assessed commit eaf86d9, 59 Node tests, four DOM journeys, and 32/32 deterministic cases cover retrieval, routing, approval, retry, stale revisions, duplicate execution, and visible recovery states.
methodology.boundary: Tests use fictional discharge material and synthetic Synthea history. A recorded live-agent attempt returned HTTP 401 before an answer, so live-agent reliability, clinical validation, and production integrations remain unverified.

role: Four-person hackathon project. The repository assigns work across data/retrieval, agent/tools, product experience, and reliability/presentation; this case study reports the combined product and its verified behavior.

pageSections.title: A discharge packet becomes a coordinated recovery plan
pageSections.description: Homeward organizes medications, appointments, warning signs, caregiver tasks, source-linked answers, and approval requests in one timeline.
pageSections.context: The prototype uses fictional discharge instructions and synthetic Synthea history to exercise successful actions, review states, and recoverable failures.

pageSections.title: Patients and caregivers can see the next task, owner, and source
pageSections.description: The primary view groups discharge tasks by urgency and shows the patient, caregiver, or care-team responsibility attached to each item.
pageSections.caption: Fictional discharge journey used for deterministic product tests.

pageSections.title: How a discharge question reaches an approved action
pageSections.description: The orchestration flow separates retrieval, specialist work, patient-facing output, and approval.

items.title: Read the discharge source
items.body: Retrieve the relevant instruction, medication, appointment, or warning sign from the patient packet.

items.title: Route the task
items.body: Send the request to the specialist workflow responsible for scheduling, medication, education, or follow-up.

items.title: Show the source and proposal
items.body: Display the cited instruction, proposed action, responsible person, and current status.

items.title: Request human approval
items.body: Hold consequential actions until the patient, caregiver, or reviewer confirms the proposal.

items.title: Complete or recover
items.body: Record the completed step or expose a retry and escalation path when a dependency fails.

pageSections.title: Four controls keep the workflow reviewable

items.label: Grounding
items.title: Answers cite discharge material
items.body: Patient-facing guidance points to the source instruction used by the workflow.

items.label: Routing
items.title: Specialists have bounded responsibilities
items.body: Each task type reaches a defined workflow with an explicit handoff.

items.label: Approval
items.title: Consequential actions wait
items.body: A reviewer sees the proposed change before execution.

items.label: Recovery
items.title: Failures remain visible
items.body: Retry and escalation states identify the failed dependency and next action.

pageSections.title: 59 tests, four DOM journeys, and 32 deterministic cases verify the prototype
pageSections.description: The assessed commit covers source retrieval, specialist routing, approvals, stale revisions, duplicate execution, activity history, retry, and visible recovery.
pageSections.markdown: The deterministic suite passed 32/32 cases at assessed commit eaf86d9. A separate live-agent trial failed authentication with HTTP 401 before producing an answer, so the portfolio treats live-model reliability as unresolved. All patient data and discharge materials are fictional; clinical review and production integrations have not been completed.
